primary.use: Layer B exposure–response (heat → all-cause mortality) for Delhi
primary.citation: Hajat S, Armstrong BG, Gouveia N, Wilkinson P. Mortality displacement of heat-related deaths: a comparison of Delhi, São Paulo, and London. Epidemiology. 2005;16(5):613–620.
primary.source_consulted: PubMed abstract (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16135936/). The full text is paywalled and was not consulted, so no table or page number is available; values are from the Results section of the abstract.
quotes: For each city, an increase in all-cause mortality was observed with same-day (lag 0) and previous day (lag 1) temperatures greater than a threshold of 20 degrees C.
The risk summed over the course of 28 days was 2.4% (95% confidence interval = 0.1 to 4.7%) per degree greater than the heat threshold in Delhi
In Delhi, an excess was apparent up to 3 weeks after exposure, after which a deficit was observed that offset just part of the overall excess.

values.exposure_metric_as_stated: daily ambient temperature (abstract: 'daily mortality data in relation to daily ambient temperature')
values.lag_note: cumulative effect summed over lags 0–27, net of mortality displacement

caveats: Exposure is air temperature, not WBGT; the model is applied on its native metric after mapping forecast WBGT to daily mean air temperature (see ml/outputs/layerB.json). Whether the study used the daily mean or another daily statistic is not stated in the abstract; daily mean is assumed.
The underlying Delhi data are from the early 1990s; vulnerability, health care and population have changed since.

secondary.use: Cross-check of heatwave risk and the Delhi baseline death count
secondary.citation: de Bont J, Nori-Sarma A, Stafoggia M, et al. Impact of heatwaves on all-cause mortality in India: A comprehensive multi-city study. Environment International. 2024;184:108461.

quotes.text: temperatures above 97th percentile for 2-consecutive days was associated with a 14.7 % (95 %CI, 10.3; 19.3) increase in daily mortality

quotes.columns: City | Time period | Daily deaths (mean) | N° of heatwaves | Heatwaves per year (mean) | Day in the season from start summer (mean days) | Length heatwave (mean days) | Intensity heatwave (mean heatwave temperature in °C and (%))

quotes.text: We obtained all-cause mortality counts for ten cities in India (2008-2019) and estimated daily mean temperatures from satellite data.

values.heatwave_definition: daily mean temperature above the city's 97th annual percentile on 2 consecutive days; pooled over 10 cities
